title: The old New Orleans players were skilled musicians
summary: Discussion of Keppard's power and why Mutt Carey, Dodds, Nicholas and others were not fakers.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Oh. That he had. Even on those old primitive records, his power is fantastic. He was, he was, he was terrific. You say he was the best hot trumpet you've heard? Yes, and with power, you know, hit. Norman told me that it wasn't the kind that hurt your ears.
It just went through the roof.

It wasn't a blasting, loud trumpet player. You know, those guys, they had knowledge of the instrument. Yeah. They had knowledge of the instrument. They played it, they played the, well, I can't say the word in English. They played it with the intelligence of the instrument.
They didn't, they didn't overblow and blast out of the note. They just played with indivility of the instrument.
There's so much ignorance, willfulness of those men. I mean, we think we can play on their stupidity. They weren't stupid. They were musicians. No.

No, they're just the people of today. The registration is different from that time and today. It's better to then than it was then. And people just misjudge guys like Mud Carrey, Freddie Caput, and I would say also Spider, which he didn't continue to play. And I've had the opportunity to hear Kid Punch when I was in New Orleans then.
Oh, you heard Punch then. Yeah.
And Punch was just, I mean, he was, it was crazy. But he was doing so much. Those guys, like, I never met a senior at all. I met Dodd. I met Benny Bigard.
Did you meet Dodds when he was playing with Ori?
Yes. And I met Nicholas. People have a wrong conception of those guys. They think they were fakers.
Did Nick remember you from those days?
No, I never, no. I just wondered if you ran across him. I was too young. I don't think he's, I don't know how old he is, but he's not too old.
